personas.label: Workspace owners

personas.label: Collaboration platform managers

examDifficulty.heading: Is the Slack Administrator Exam Hard?
examDifficulty.summary: This exam covers many parts of Slack administration: workspaces and Enterprise Grid, user accounts, app approvals, security and compliance, and Workflow Builder.
bullets: 60 scored questions in 105 minutes, plus up to five unscored questions that do not count.
60 scored questions in 105 minutes, plus up to five unscored questions that do not count.
Wide coverage. Review settings, permissions, Enterprise Grid, Slack Connect, security, compliance, and automation.
Hands-on admin work helps. Practice SSO, user provisioning, and app approvals in Slack.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: You are ready when you can explain how SSO and user provisioning work, who can create channels or invite guests, how to approve apps, and how retention works. Aim for at least 75% on practice tests before booking.

examFormat.heading: Slack Administrator Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: The exam is proctored online or at a test center. Many questions describe a company requirement and ask which Slack setting or feature meets it.
examFormat.scenarioPercent: A question may ask how to keep messages for seven years or stop guests from joining private channels. Identify the requirement, then choose the setting that controls it.
bestWayToPass: Learn roles and access: Review Primary Owner, Owner, Admin, Member, and guest permissions.
Understand Enterprise Grid: Learn what changes when several workspaces share central organization settings.
Study security and compliance: Review SSO, SCIM, session length, retention, legal holds, data loss prevention, and device controls.
Practice Workflow Builder: Make a simple workflow that collects information and posts it to a channel. Learn its triggers and steps.

certificationCard.description: This exam covers Slack setup and daily administration: workspaces, channels, user accounts, roles, permissions, apps, security, compliance, Enterprise Grid, and Workflow Builder. The exam is 60 scored questions in 105 minutes, with a 65% pass mark, weighted towards Governance, Security and Compliance (22%) and App and AI Administration and Automations (20%).

keyConcepts.h2: Slack Administrator: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: Workspaces, Channels, and Roles
blocks.body: A **workspace** is the Slack environment people use to work together. **Channels** hold conversations. Public channels are open to workspace members, private channels require an invitation, and shared channels connect to another organization. A **Primary Owner** can transfer ownership or delete the workspace. **Owners** and **Admins** manage settings; **Members** use the workspace. **Multi-channel guests** can join several assigned channels, while **single-channel guests** can join one. Admins can control who creates or archives channels, who invites guests, and which channels new members join.

blocks.heading: Permissions, Security, and Compliance
blocks.body: Match each security need to the right setting. **SSO** with SAML lets people sign in through the company identity provider and can be required. **SCIM provisioning** creates or deactivates accounts through that system. **Session duration** controls how often users sign in again. **Retention settings** control how long messages and files are kept. **Legal holds** preserve a person’s data for a legal matter, while **data loss prevention (DLP)** can detect sensitive content. **Enterprise Key Management** gives the company control of its encryption keys. Mobile device management controls access from phones.

blocks.heading: Apps and Integrations
blocks.body: Apps add features to Slack, and admins need to keep them secure while allowing useful work. Require **app approval** so an admin reviews requests before installation, and maintain an approved app list. Admins can review installed apps and the access scopes they have, then remove apps when needed. Apply the same checks to internal apps. Know whether an app is installed for one user, a workspace, or the full organization. Enterprise Grid can apply app policies across the organization.

blocks.heading: Enterprise Grid Administration
blocks.body: **Enterprise Grid** connects several workspaces under one organization. It suits large companies where business units need separate spaces and central administration. Settings such as SSO, retention, and app approval can be managed at the **organization level**. **Org-wide channels** can share updates across workspaces. People can join more than one workspace with the same account. Choose Grid when a company needs both separation between teams and shared control.

blocks.heading: Workflow Builder and Automation
blocks.body: **Workflow Builder** lets people automate simple tasks in Slack without code. A workflow can start when someone clicks a shortcut, joins a channel, or when a scheduled time arrives. Steps can post a message, collect information in a **form**, or connect to another app. Common uses include request forms, onboarding checklists, and approvals. Admins should decide who can publish workflows and review unused ones. Use a tool such as Salesforce Flow when the process needs to change data in another system or apply complex rules.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Salesforce Slack Administrator Exam
scenarioTips.intro: Questions usually state a business or security need and ask which setting meets it. Check whether the setting applies to one workspace or to the whole organization.

blocks.heading: Workspaces and Enterprise Grid
blocks.body: A single workspace fits many companies. Enterprise Grid helps when business units need separate workspaces with central administration.

blocks.heading: Channel Rules
blocks.body: Decide who can create or archive channels, set default channels, and use naming rules that help people find the right place.

blocks.heading: Apps and Security
blocks.body: Require app approval, maintain an approved list, and review each app’s access scopes.

blocks.heading: Retention and Compliance
blocks.body: Retention sets how long messages are kept. Legal holds preserve data for a case. DLP can detect sensitive information.

blocks.heading: Accounts and Sign-In
blocks.body: Use SSO for sign-in and SCIM to create or remove accounts automatically through the company identity system.

nextCertsAfter.heading: Next Certifications to Consider
nextCertsAfter.intro: Build on your Slack administration knowledge with these related Salesforce credentials:

sampleQuestions.question: What is the main role of a Certified Slack Administrator?
options: Develop custom Slack apps and publish them to the Slack Marketplace for other companies
Implement, configure, and manage Slack, and recommend useful policies and features
sampleQuestions.explanation: Certified Slack Administrators set up and manage Slack. They also recommend policies and features that help teams work well.
whyWrong: The role includes much more than developing apps.
Creating marketing campaigns is not Slack administration.
Salesforce CRM administration is a separate role.

sampleQuestions.question: Where do admins usually manage Slack settings for the whole organization?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Admins use Slack Admin or Org settings for workspace and organization-wide controls.
whyWrong: Salesforce settings control Salesforce, not Slack.
Channel settings do not control the whole organization.
Email Studio is part of Marketing Cloud, not Slack administration.

sampleQuestions.question: Which Slack controls can limit who creates channels or invites guests?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Admin policies and permissions can control channel creation, guest invitations, and other workspace actions.
whyWrong: Emoji reactions are for communication, not workspace access.
Search filters help users find content.
Bookmarks save content; they do not control access.

sampleQuestions.question: What does Slack Connect let organizations do?
options: Connect a shared email inbox to a channel so that messages arrive in Slack
Work securely with people from other organizations in shared channels
sampleQuestions.explanation: Slack Connect supports secure collaboration with external organizations through shared channels.
whyWrong: Slack Connect is for cross-organization collaboration, not email alone.
CPQ quotes are unrelated to Slack Connect.
Slack Connect is designed to work across organizations, not only inside one.

sampleQuestions.question: Which recommendation can help a team work better in Slack?
options: Use workflows, a clear channel structure, and suitable settings
Limit each team to a single channel so that every conversation stays in one place
sampleQuestions.explanation: Workflows, clear channel names, and useful settings can help teams work more efficiently.
whyWrong: Turning off every integration may remove useful tools.
Removing search makes it harder to find information.
One channel may not fit all team discussions.

sampleQuestions.question: What is Slack Enterprise Grid for?
options: Connecting company email to Slack so that messages are delivered to selected channels
Connecting several workspaces under one organization with central administration
sampleQuestions.explanation: Enterprise Grid lets large organizations connect and centrally manage multiple Slack workspaces.
whyWrong: Enterprise Grid does more than reporting.
Email is a separate feature.
Enterprise Grid supports multiple connected workspaces.

sampleQuestions.question: Which Slack feature lets people build simple automated workflows without code?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Workflow Builder lets people create automated workflows for common tasks without writing code.
whyWrong: Slack Connect is for external collaboration.
Channel management does not build automated workflows.
Search helps find content.

sampleQuestions.question: What does a Slack message retention policy control?
options: Who is allowed to join a private channel
How long messages and files are kept
sampleQuestions.explanation: A retention policy defines how long workspace messages and files remain available before Slack removes them.
whyWrong: Channel names identify channels but do not control data retention.
Channel membership is a separate access control.
Integrations are configured separately from retention.

sampleQuestions.question: Which policies can help preserve Slack data when employees leave?
options: Data retention and eDiscovery export policies
Notification preferences for each member's devices
sampleQuestions.explanation: Retention and eDiscovery policies help an organization preserve and recover data.
whyWrong: Theme settings change appearance, not data retention.
Emoji settings change reactions, not data retention.
Notification preferences are personal settings, not data retention controls.

sampleQuestions.question: Which Slack feature lets people in separate workspaces collaborate in one shared channel?
options: A public channel inside one workspace that every member is able to find and join
A channel shared by multiple Slack workspaces for cross-organization work
sampleQuestions.explanation: A shared channel connects Slack workspaces so different organizations can work together.
whyWrong: A large membership does not make a channel shared across workspaces.
A public channel is not necessarily shared with another workspace.
Integrations do not define whether a channel is shared.

sampleQuestions.question: How can Slack admins control which apps members can install?
options: Channel creation settings in workspace permissions
App management policies and approved app lists
sampleQuestions.explanation: App management policies and approved app lists let admins control which apps members can use.
whyWrong: Channel creation settings control channels, not apps.
Invitation settings control who can join, not app installation.
Search helps find messages; it does not control installed apps.

sampleQuestions.question: What can Slack Analytics help admins understand?
options: Email open and click statistics for campaigns
sampleQuestions.explanation: Slack Analytics helps admins review how people use Slack, including adoption and engagement.
whyWrong: Slack Analytics focuses on Slack usage, not email statistics.
It provides more than a message count.
Sales data is not Slack usage analytics.

sampleQuestions.question: Which tools help admins manage many Slack users at once?
options: Email invitations sent one by one
Manual setup of each user account in turn
sampleQuestions.explanation: SCIM provisioning and directory sync can create, update, and remove user accounts at scale.
whyWrong: Email invitations are not an efficient way to manage a large user base.
Manual changes are difficult to maintain at scale.
Channel invitations manage channel membership, not organization-wide user accounts.

sampleQuestions.question: Why might an organization use Slack compliance exports?
options: To create ordinary usage reports for managers and team leads
To export messages and files for legal or compliance needs
sampleQuestions.explanation: Compliance exports can provide message and file data for legal, regulatory, or compliance reviews.
whyWrong: Compliance exports are for data export, not ordinary reporting.
They support more than file backup.
Slack Connect is used to share channels.

sampleQuestions.question: Which Slack Connect action needs approval from both organizations?
options: Joining an existing channel in your own workspace
Creating a shared channel between workspaces
sampleQuestions.explanation: Creating a shared channel requires approval from admins in both organizations.
whyWrong: Once the channel exists, sending a message does not require that setup approval.
Adding an emoji is a normal channel action.
Joining an existing channel is not the cross-organization setup step.

sampleQuestions.question: An admin wants to turn on AI-powered channel recaps and thread summaries for their org. Where does that get configured?
options: Slack AI settings, managed at the admin level with permissions assigned to users
There is no admin control, so every member has to turn it on individually for themselves
Only Slack's own support team can enable it
It's automatically on for every plan with no setting
sampleQuestions.explanation: Slack AI features like channel recaps, thread summaries, and AI-powered search are turned on and governed at the admin level, with user permissions assigned from there.
whyWrong: Individual members don't control org-wide AI feature access, that's an admin setting.
Admins, not Slack support, manage their own org's AI feature access.
AI features are plan-gated and admin-controlled, not automatically on everywhere.

sampleQuestions.question: A large company wants new hires automatically added to Slack the moment they're created in the company's identity provider, with no manual admin step. What provisioning method fits?
options: Manual invites sent one at a time
Asking each new hire to self-register with a public signup link
sampleQuestions.explanation: SCIM provisioning (or JIT provisioning tied to SSO login) automates account creation and deactivation from the identity provider, with no manual admin step needed per user.
whyWrong: Manual invites don't scale and require an admin action for every new hire.
Public self-registration isn't a secure, governed provisioning method for an enterprise workspace.
A periodic CSV upload isn't automatic and introduces a delay between hire and access.

sampleQuestions.question: What's a common responsibility that both the Admin and Owner roles share in Slack?
options: Day-to-day workspace management tasks like managing members and channels
Only Owners can ever manage members, Admins cannot
Only Admins can see billing information
Owner and Admin are exactly the same role, with no distinction of any kind between them
sampleQuestions.explanation: Admins and Owners share common day-to-day responsibilities like managing members and channels, though Owners typically hold additional org-level authority such as billing and plan changes.
whyWrong: Admins can also manage members, that's a shared responsibility, not an Owner-exclusive one.
Billing is more commonly an Owner-level responsibility, not Admin-exclusive.
The roles share responsibilities but aren't identical, Owner carries extra authority.

sampleQuestions.question: A team wants to track action items from a project directly inside Slack, assignable to members with due dates, instead of using channel messages alone. Which feature fits?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Slack Lists let teams track structured items like tasks, with fields such as assignee and due date, right inside Slack.
whyWrong: A Canvas is better for structured reference content and documentation, not task tracking with assignees and due dates.
A channel topic is a short description line, it can't track individual action items.
A pinned message highlights one message, it doesn't provide structured, assignable task tracking.

sampleQuestions.question: A company manages which Slack workspaces a department can access through groups defined in their identity provider. After updating those IdP groups, what should the admin expect?
options: Slack workspace access updates to reflect the IdP group changes, once synced
Nothing changes in Slack until every affected user has been manually re-invited by an admin
The IdP groups only affect email, not Slack
IdP groups can only be set up once and never changed
sampleQuestions.explanation: When an org manages workspace access through IdP groups, updating those groups and syncing them updates who has access in Slack, without manual re-invitations for each person.
whyWrong: Manual re-invitation defeats the point of IdP-group-based access management.
IdP groups used for this purpose govern Slack workspace access, not just email.
IdP groups can be updated as org structure changes, they aren't a one-time, permanent setup.
